newsitem.title: UK: BOC at record on disposal hopes.
newsitem.headline: BOC at record on disposal hopes.

text.p: BOC Group Plc shares hit a record high on Wednesday as the market reacted enthusiastically to the planned sale of its Ohmeda health care business, which could raise some one billion stg.

BOC shares were up 72-1/2p or 6.8 percent at 11.45 by 1040 GMT, after rising as high as 11.49-1/2 -- surpassing its previous peak of 11.07 stg set July 18, though dealers pointed out that volume was a relatively modest 1.1 million shares.
"It is not a very marketable stock so the price move is a bit exaggerated," said one dealer, "but they are getting rid of a unit that has been a bit of a thorn in their side."
Traders and analysts said the disposal would take BOC out of a relatively low-growth business and allow it to pursue growth opportunities in industrial gases.
"They will be in a position to chase even harder the growth opportunities in their gases operations," said Peter Cartwright, analyst at Williams de Broe.
Cartwright pointed out that with gearing at around 60 percent, BOC could have been forced into a rights issue or other fund-raising exercise to finance expansion plans.

BOC said proceeds from the disposal would not burn a hole in its pocket though it did not rule out acquisitions. Ohmeda's turnover in the last year was 506 million stg and operating profit was 53 million stg.
"This could be one of those deals when BOC may be able to sell for a pretty high price and it would still be a good price for the right purchaser," said Paul Diggle, analyst at SocGen.
Diggle said another healthcare group could achieve cost savings to justify a purchase price of as much as 1 billion stg.
For BOC, the savings in its interest bill could almost offset the loss in Ohmeda's profits, he said.
